From 068bb1a75a94eacfaaacf3b0ecf4feb349fa8e13 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Steve Glendinning <steve.glendinning@shawell.net>
Date: Fri, 30 Nov 2012 05:55:51 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] smsc95xx: fix smsc_crc return type

This patch fixes a bug introduced in bbd9f9e which could prevent
some wakeups from working correctly if multiple wol options were
selected.

This helper function calculates a 16-bit crc and shifts it into
either the high or low 16 bits of a u32 so the caller can or it
directly into place.  The function previously had a u16 return
type so would always have returned zero when filter was odd.

Signed-off-by: Steve Glendinning <steve.glendinning@shawell.net>
Reported-by: Bjorn Mork <bjorn@mork.no>
Cc: Joe Perches <joe@perches.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

diff --git a/drivers/net/usb/smsc95xx.c b/drivers/net/usb/smsc95xx.c
index 064df1af0df3..b9eb490afa45 100644
--- a/drivers/net/usb/smsc95xx.c
+++ b/drivers/net/usb/smsc95xx.c
@@ -1074,9 +1074,10 @@ static void smsc95xx_unbind(struct usbnet *dev, struct usb_interface *intf)
 	}
 }
 
-static u16 smsc_crc(const u8 *buffer, size_t len, int filter)
+static u32 smsc_crc(const u8 *buffer, size_t len, int filter)
 {
-	return bitrev16(crc16(0xFFFF, buffer, len)) << ((filter % 2) * 16);
+	u32 crc = bitrev16(crc16(0xFFFF, buffer, len));
+	return crc << ((filter % 2) * 16);
 }
 
 static int smsc95xx_enable_phy_wakeup_interrupts(struct usbnet *dev, u16 mask)
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/net/usb/smsc95xx.c`**
- The return type of the function `smsc_crc` was changed from `u16` to `u32`.
- The implementation of the `smsc_crc` function was modified to store the result of `bitrev16(crc16(0xFFFF, buffer, len))` in a variable of type `u32` before shifting it. The return statement was updated to return this `u32` value after the shift operation.

### Relationships
The modification in the `smsc_crc` function's return type and implementation directly addresses a bug introduced in a previous commit (bbd9f9e). The bug caused the function to always return zero when the `filter` parameter was odd, which could lead to incorrect behavior in wakeup functionality when multiple wake-on-LAN (WOL) options were selected. By changing the return type to `u32`, the function can now correctly return the calculated CRC value, thus fixing the bug and ensuring proper operation of the wakeup feature.

Here is the commit message:
smsc95xx: fix smsc_crc return type

This patch fixes a bug introduced in bbd9f9e which could prevent
some wakeups from working correctly if multiple wol options were
selected.

This helper function calculates a 16-bit crc and shifts it into
either the high or low 16 bits of a u32 so the caller can or it
directly into place.  The function previously had a u16 return
type so would always have returned zero when filter was odd.

Signed-off-by: Steve Glendinning <steve.glendinning@shawell.net>
Reported-by: Bjorn Mork <bjorn@mork.no>
Cc: Joe Perches <joe@perches.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the `smsc_crc` function having a return type of `u16`, which limited its output range. As a result, when the `filter` parameter was odd, the function would always return zero due to the truncation of the higher bits, leading to incorrect behavior in wakeup functionality when multiple wake-on-LAN options were selected.

Here is the patch:
 
-static u16 smsc_crc(const u8 *buffer, size_t len, int filter)
+static u32 smsc_crc(const u8 *buffer, size_t len, int filter)
 {
-	return bitrev16(crc16(0xFFFF, buffer, len)) << ((filter % 2) * 16);
+	u32 crc = bitrev16(crc16(0xFFFF, buffer, len));
+	return crc << ((filter % 2) * 16);
 }

The `smsc_crc` function had a return type of `u16`, which limited the output to 16 bits. When the `filter` parameter was odd, the higher bits of the CRC value were truncated, causing the function to always return zero. This incorrect return value led to failures in wakeup functionality when multiple wake-on-LAN options were selected.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
+static u32 smsc_crc(const u8 *buffer, size_t len, int filter)
```

Reason:
The return type of the `smsc_crc` function was changed to `u32`, allowing it to return a full 32-bit value. This change ensures that the higher bits are preserved, preventing the truncation issue when the `filter` is odd. As a result, the function can now correctly calculate and return the CRC value, fixing the wakeup functionality.
